chunks: As for what Mu‘āwiyah ibn Ḥukaym narrated from Ibn al-Mughīrah, from Muthannā ibn ‘Abd al-Salām, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
I said to him: I scratched my skin and blood came out from it. So he said: “If it gathers to the measure of a chickpea, then wash it; otherwise, no.”

So this is to be understood as recommendation rather than obligation. What indicates that is what has preceded from the reports, and that whenever it does not reach the amount of a dirham, salat in the garment in which that blood is found is permissible; and this also indicates it.

In the sharī‘ah, salat was only permitted with some specific kinds of blood in small amounts because of the proof established for it, namely what we have already presented from the reports. As for menstrual blood, impurity is established in its small amount and its large amount, so the obligation of removing it must be established in every case, so that a person may enter into salat with certainty after removing it; and this too is indicated by the evidence.

key_terms.الدِّرْهَمَ: a dirham-sized measure used as a legal threshold for blood amount
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), whose validity is discussed in relation to blood on clothing
key_terms.النَّجَاسَةُ: ritual impurity established in relation to blood
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; an act encouraged but not obligatory
key_terms.حِمَّصَةٍ: the measure of a chickpea, used here as a small unit of amount
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood that emerges from the body and affects rulings of ritual purity
key_terms.دَمُ الْحَيْضِ: menstrual blood, treated here as requiring removal in all amounts

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a small amount of blood on the body or garment before salat?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling on small amounts of blood resulting from scratching the skin and explains that washing such blood is understood here as recommended, not obligatory, when it is below a certain amount. It further distinguishes this from menstrual blood, whose impurity applies whether little or much, making its removal obligatory before salat.
